operational_contract: Direct posting requires an approved publishing scope and user authorization.
Unaudited clients are restricted and must not be treated as public-production capable.
Publishing returns a publish identifier and requires status verification.
The Posts API is versioned and sunset versions must not be used.
Organization publishing requires approved access and appropriate organization roles.
A successful create response exposes a remote post identifier.
Post creation uses the current X API post-management contract.
ContentFlow must persist the returned remote identifier before counting success.
Retries require a ContentFlow idempotency guard because remote duplicate semantics are platform-specific.
Publishing eligibility, media constraints, permissions, and account prerequisites must be checked from the current official contract.
A container or submission state is not equivalent to a confirmed public post.
ContentFlow must read back the remote state before recording content_published.

limitations: This cache is a source contract, not an OAuth credential or proof of live publishing.
Platform rules may change before the weekly review date.
No entry is promoted into production behavior without connector tests and reviewer approval.
